scenes.text: Every person, place, animal and thing has a name.
A naming word is called a noun.
Meena and teacher are names of people. They are nouns.
School and park are names of places. Cat and parrot are names of animals.
Ball, book and chair are names of things. They are nouns too.
In the sentence 'The dog sleeps on the mat', dog and mat are nouns.

solution.explanation: A bird is a living thing, so 'bird' is a noun.

body.prompt: Which word is the name of a place?

solution.explanation: A market is a place, so 'market' is a noun.
A doctor is a person, so 'doctor' is a noun.

body.prompt: Which word is a noun in: 'Ravi eats a mango.'?

solution.explanation: A mango is a thing, so 'mango' is a noun. 'Ravi' is a noun too.

body.prompt: Which word is NOT a noun?

solution.explanation: 'Sing' is an action, so it is not a noun.
An elephant is an animal, so its name is a noun.

body.prompt: 'Swim' is a noun in: 'Fish swim in water.'

solution.explanation: 'Swim' is an action word here. 'Fish' and 'water' are the nouns.

body.prompt: The ___ is flying in the sky.

solution.explanation: 'Kite' is a thing, a noun, that can fly in the sky.

body.prompt: A naming word is called a ___.

solution.explanation: Naming words are nouns.

body.prompt: Match each noun to what it names.

solution.explanation: A teacher is a person, a garden is a place, a parrot is an animal and a chair is a thing.

body.text: Ravi has a red kite. On Sunday, he goes to the park with his sister Asha. The wind is strong. Ravi runs and the kite goes up, up, up. It flies over the tall trees. Asha claps her hands. "Your kite is like a bird!" she says. Ravi smiles and holds the string tight. When the sun goes down, they walk home happily.

scenes.text: We do many things every day. We run, jump, read and eat.
Words that tell us what someone does are action words.
An action word is called a verb.
In 'The baby cries', cries is a verb. It tells us what the baby does.
In 'Birds fly in the sky', fly is a verb.
Clap your hands! Clap is a verb too.

solution.explanation: 'Jump' is an action, so it is a verb.

body.prompt: Which word is the verb in: 'Neha reads a book.'?

solution.explanation: 'Reads' tells us what Neha does.

body.prompt: Choose the verb: 'The cow eats grass.'

solution.explanation: 'Eats' is the action of the cow.

body.prompt: Which action can a bird do?

solution.explanation: 'Fly' is an action word.

body.prompt: Which word is NOT a verb?

solution.explanation: 'Apple' is a thing, a noun, not an action.
Running is an action, so 'run' is a verb.
A ball is a thing, so 'ball' is a noun.
'Play' tells us what the children do.
'Swim' is what fish do.
A dog barks, a cook cooks and a singer sings.

body.text: Dark clouds fill the sky. Soon, big drops of rain begin to fall. Meera opens the window and looks outside. The trees dance in the wind. Frogs jump in the puddles and sing loudly. Meera's mother makes hot pakoras in the kitchen. Meera sits near the window with a cup of milk. She loves the smell of wet earth.

scenes.text: Some words tell us more about a noun.
They can tell us the colour, size, shape or number of something.
These describing words are called adjectives.
A red ball. Red tells us the colour of the ball.
A big elephant. Big tells us the size of the elephant.
Two cats. Two tells us how many cats there are.

body.prompt: Which word is a describing word?

solution.explanation: 'Tall' tells us how something looks, so it is an adjective.

body.prompt: Which word is the adjective in: 'I have a yellow pencil.'?

solution.explanation: 'Yellow' tells us the colour of the pencil.
'Small' tells us the size of something.

body.prompt: Find the adjective: 'There are five ducks in the pond.'

solution.explanation: 'Five' tells us how many ducks there are.
'Hot' and 'cold' are opposites.

body.prompt: In 'a soft pillow', the word 'soft' is an adjective.

solution.explanation: 'Soft' describes the pillow.
'Run' is an action word, a verb.
'Sweet' describes how the mango tastes.
Elephants are big animals.

body.prompt: Match each word to its opposite.

solution.explanation: Big–small, fast–slow, happy–sad.

body.text: Every year, a big fair comes to our village. There are colourful stalls full of toys, bangles and sweets. A tall giant wheel turns slowly near the pond. My little brother wants a shiny balloon, so Father buys him a blue one. We eat hot jalebis and drink cold lassi. At night, bright lights shine everywhere. It is the happiest day of the year.

scenes.text: One cat. Two cats. Can you see the difference?
A word for one thing is singular. A word for many things is plural.
We often add s to make a plural: book becomes books, pen becomes pens.
Some words take es: box becomes boxes, bus becomes buses.
Some words change: man becomes men, child becomes children.
Look around you. Name one thing, then many things.

solution.explanation: We add s to book to make books.
Words ending in x take es: boxes.
Child changes to children.
'Flower' means one flower, so it is singular.
Man changes to men.
Words ending in s take es: buses.
We just add s: pens.
Three means many, so we use the plural 'apples'.

body.prompt: Please give me one ___ of milk.

solution.explanation: One means singular, so we use 'cup'.

body.prompt: Match each word to its plural.

solution.explanation: Dish–dishes, tooth–teeth, girl–girls, mouse–mice.

body.text: On Saturday, Grandmother takes Arjun to the vegetable market. There are many shops in a long row. One shop has red tomatoes and green chillies. Another shop has potatoes, onions and carrots. Grandmother buys two kilos of potatoes and some bananas. Arjun carries the bags. The shopkeeper gives Arjun a sweet guava. "Thank you, uncle," says Arjun with a big smile.

Tara plants a little seed in a pot. She gives it water every morning. She keeps the pot in the sun. One day, she sees a tiny green leaf. "My seed is growing!" she shouts. Day by day, the plant grows taller. After many weeks, a pretty yellow flower opens. Tara is very proud of her plant.

scenes.text: Every sentence begins with a capital letter.
A sentence that tells us something ends with a full stop. It looks like a small dot.
Example: The sun is hot. This sentence tells us something.
A sentence that asks something ends with a question mark.
Example: Where is my bag? This sentence asks a question.
Names of people and places also begin with capital letters, like Riya and Delhi.

body.prompt: Which mark ends this sentence: 'What is your name'

solution.explanation: It asks something, so it ends with a question mark.

body.prompt: Which mark ends this sentence: 'I like to read books'

solution.explanation: It tells us something, so it ends with a full stop.
It begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
Names of places, like Mumbai, begin with a capital letter.
'Can you swim?' asks something and ends with a question mark.

body.prompt: A person's name, like Riya, begins with a capital letter.

solution.explanation: Names of people always begin with a capital letter.
It asks something, so it should end with a question mark: 'How old are you?'

body.prompt: A question ends with a ___ mark.

solution.explanation: Questions end with a question mark.

body.prompt: A sentence begins with a ___ letter.

solution.explanation: Every sentence begins with a capital letter.

body.prompt: Match each sentence to the mark it needs at the end.

solution.explanation: A question needs a question mark; a telling sentence needs a full stop.

body.text: Kabir and his family are going to Jaipur by train. The station is very busy. People carry bags and boxes. A loud whistle blows and the train starts to move. Kabir sits near the window. He sees green fields, cows and small houses. "Are we there yet?" he asks. Mother laughs and gives him a book to read. In the evening, the train reaches Jaipur.
